en.name: Dried udon noodles
en.summary: Dried udon and its thinner relatives, sōmen and hiyamugi, are wheat flour, salt and water, rolled or extruded and dried. Sealed and kept cool and dry they run about 2 years from purchase and about 1 year once opened. Those figures are borrowed from dry pasta; the storage rule itself comes from the Japanese dried-noodle trade's own labelling guideline.
en.pantry: The rule printed on the packs is the one to follow: keep dried noodles out of direct sunlight, heat and damp. That gives about 2 years from purchase in an unopened pack, and about 1 year once opened and resealed or decanted into an airtight jar. The same guideline warns that dried noodles pick up strong smells, so store them away from spices, soap and detergent. Dried noodles carry no preservative at all — their keeping quality is entirely the low moisture, roughly a tenth of their weight, which is also why a humid kitchen will let them mould or draw pantry insects.
en.fridge: Dried udon does not go in the fridge; it is a dry good and a fridge is a humid place. Cooked udon is a different food and is a wet starch: cool it quickly, keep it covered at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and reheat it thoroughly. Do not leave a pot of cooked noodles standing warm on the stove for the afternoon — cooked noodles belong to the same family as cooked rice, where holding them warm is the thing that causes trouble.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for dried udon, and none is needed: a sealed pack in a cool, dry cupboard already outlasts most households' appetite for it. Freezing the dry bundles brings condensation and no benefit. Cooked udon, by contrast, freezes genuinely well in single portions — that is the form worth putting in the freezer, though no published figure for it is offered here.
spoilage: A musty or stale smell, or a smell picked up from soap, spices or detergent nearby.
Bundles that bend instead of snapping cleanly.
Visible mould, usually in the middle of a bundle that took up damp.
Webbing, small moths or fine dust in a pack left open in a humid kitchen.
tips: Reseal or decant into an airtight jar as soon as the pack is opened.
Keep noodles well away from spices, soap and cleaning products.
Store them somewhere dry and dark rather than above the hob.
Freeze cooked udon in single portions; do not freeze the dry noodles.

faq.q: How long do dried udon noodles keep?
faq.a: About 2 years from purchase in a sealed pack, and about 1 year once opened and kept airtight.
No. What keeps them is the low moisture content, which is why damp storage is the thing that ruins them.
Freeze cooked udon in portions — it works well. Freezing the dry noodles achieves nothing and risks condensation.

zh.name: 乾烏龍麵
zh.summary: 乾烏龍麵和它較細的親戚素麵、冷麥，成分就是小麥粉、鹽和水，壓延或擠出後乾燥。密封、陰涼乾燥保存，從購買日起算約 2 年，開封後約 1 年。這兩個數字借自乾燥義大利麵；保存規則本身則來自日本乾麵同業的標示指引。
zh.pantry: 照包裝上印的規則做就對了：避開陽光直射、高溫與潮濕。這樣未開封從購買日起算約 2 年，開封後封緊或倒進密封罐約 1 年。同一份指引也提醒乾麵很會吸附強烈氣味，所以要遠離香料、肥皂和清潔劑。乾麵完全不含防腐劑——它能放，靠的純粹是低含水量（大約一成），這也是為什麼潮濕的廚房會讓它發霉或招來櫥櫃害蟲。
zh.fridge: 乾烏龍麵不放冰箱；它是乾貨，而冰箱是潮濕的地方。煮過的烏龍麵是另一種食物，屬於含水澱粉：請快速降溫、加蓋放 4 °C 以下，復熱要確實。不要讓一鍋煮好的麵在爐子上溫溫地放一下午——熟麵和熟飯是同一類，「保持微溫」正是會出事的那件事。
zh.freezer: 乾烏龍麵沒有給冷凍期限，也不需要：密封放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃，本來就比大多數家庭想吃它的時間長。把乾麵束冷凍只會結露，沒有好處。反過來說，煮好的烏龍麵分成單份冷凍效果很好——那才是值得放冷凍庫的形式，只是本頁沒有對應的公布數字。
spoilage: 聞到霉味或陳味，或吸到了旁邊肥皂、香料、清潔劑的氣味。
麵束彎得下去而折不斷。
看得見霉，通常長在受潮麵束的中心。
在潮濕廚房開封放久，出現絲網、小蛾或細粉屑。
tips: 一開封就封緊或倒進密封罐。
麵要遠離香料、肥皂與清潔用品。
放在乾燥避光處，不要放在爐台上方。
要冷凍就凍煮好的單份烏龍麵，不要凍乾麵。

faq.a: 未開封從購買日起算約 2 年，開封後密封保存約 1 年。
沒有。讓它能放的是低含水量，所以受潮才是毀掉它的原因。
煮好的分份冷凍效果很好。乾麵冷凍沒有意義，還會有結露風險。
